title: Scientists Reveal How 60% of Medieval Stories May Have Disappeared Forever
content:
Chanson d’Aspremont (a version of the Legend of Roland). Shelfmark: Lansdowne 782. Credit: From the British Library archive. E50003-09
New simulations reveal how a medieval story’s earliest years may have determined its survival.
The medieval world may have produced far more stories of knights, legendary heroes, and epic adventures than historians will ever recover. A new study suggests that up to 60% of medieval chivalric works and more than 95% of their handwritten copies may have disappeared over the centuries.
Jean-Baptiste Camps and colleagues reached these estimates by combining computer simulations with historical evidence from approximately 2,000 medieval manuscripts spanning four centuries. Their research examines how stories survived through repeated copying, why others vanished entirely, and how much of a surviving work’s original history may be missing.
Why a Story’s First Years Could Determine Its Survival
Before the printing press, preserving a literary work depended on scribes making copies by hand. Each new manuscript could introduce accidental errors, deliberate revisions, or adaptations for different audiences. These changes accumulated across generations, producing branching family trees resembling those used to trace evolutionary relationships in biology. Scholars call these textual genealogies
stemmata
The simulations suggest that a work’s earliest years were especially critical. When only a few copies existed, the loss of those manuscripts could cause the entire text to disappear. The authors describe this vulnerable early period as a “danger zone.” Producing numerous copies soon after a work’s creation could substantially improve its chances of surviving for centuries.
The researchers tested several scenarios, including steady copying rates, declining popularity, and sudden destruction of manuscripts during a major crisis. Depending on the scenario, their models estimated that just 1.4% to 4.4% of individual manuscripts survived, illustrating how extensive the losses could have been.
Even Surviving Stories May Have Lost Their Original Versions
The disappearance of manuscripts did more than eliminate entire works. It also erased branches of the textual family trees that connect surviving copies to their origins.
The simulations indicate that surviving manuscripts often descend from later versions rather than directly preserving an author’s original text. The
Song of Roland
, one of the most famous medieval epics, may be an example. Its earliest form is probably lost, leaving scholars with later versions and rewritings that cannot fully establish what the original contained.
Historical events may have further influenced which stories endured. The Black Death, the Hundred Years’ War, and changing literary tastes could have disrupted manuscript production or contributed to the destruction of existing copies. Although the simulations demonstrate the substantial role chance can play, they do not establish which individual works disappeared because of particular historical events.
“Our results expose the fragility of cultural heritage and offer new tools to understand how randomness, historical contingencies, and human choices have shaped the legacy we inherit today,” the authors write.

title: Earth’s Oceans Were Slowly Suffocating Millions of Years Before a Devastating Mass Extinction
content:
Fossilized shells from the sedimentary rock layer. Credit: Ben Gill
As today’s oceans lose oxygen, Alaskan rocks trace a similar decline that began millions of years before the end-Triassic mass extinction.
Dinosaurs survived the end-Triassic mass extinction 201 million years ago, but roughly 60 percent of Earth’s species did not. New evidence from
Virginia Tech
geologists suggests that the crisis in the oceans began about 8 million years earlier, when oxygen levels in shallow waters started to decline.
Scientists have long linked the extinction to enormous volcanic eruptions that tore apart landmasses, warmed the planet, and triggered widespread environmental changes. As temperatures rise, rocks break down faster, releasing nutrients that contribute to increasing ocean acidity. Warmer seawater also holds less dissolved oxygen, creating conditions that can lead to oxygen-depleted dead zones where marine organisms struggle to survive.
The combination of rising acidity and falling oxygen is “kind of like a one-two punch,” said geochemist Ben Gill. “It wouldn’t have been a very happy place to be.”
Although scientists had previously found evidence of widespread marine oxygen loss around the end-Triassic extinction, much of it came from a limited geographic area. Researchers still lacked a clear understanding of when the decline began and how extensively it affected the oceans. Recent studies had also raised the possibility that environmental conditions started deteriorating far earlier than previously believed.
“It’s a 200-million-year-old cold case,” said Kayla McCabe, a former Virginia Tech geosciences graduate student and first author of the study, published in
Communications Earth & Environment
Alaska’s rocks reveal a prolonged oxygen crisis
To investigate, McCabe and her colleagues turned to sedimentary rocks at Grotto Creek in Alaska’s Wrangell–St. Elias National Park. The remote location is accessible only by small aircraft, and the team traveled there in 2017, 2019, and 2022 to collect evidence of ancient ocean conditions.
Sedimentary rocks form as layers of material accumulate over time, preserving chemical traces of the environments in which they were deposited. By comparing layers formed before, during, and after the extinction, the researchers could reconstruct how oxygen conditions changed across millions of years.
Members of a field team examine an outcrop of rock layers in Grotto Creek in Alaska’s Wrangell–St. Elias National Park in 2019. Credit: Ben Gill
The geochemical analyses revealed a prolonged deterioration rather than a sudden collapse. The earlier decline likely placed marine ecosystems under stress long before the main extinction event. Conditions then worsened considerably during the extinction itself, with the rock record showing a much more severe loss of oxygen. The findings indicate that oxygen starvation became a major contributor to the disappearance of marine species.
The earliest oxygen loss remains unexplained
What triggered the initial decline remains uncertain. The massive volcanic eruptions associated with the end-Triassic extinction have long been considered a major cause of the environmental catastrophe, but the newly identified timeline raises questions about what was happening millions of years beforehand.
“There’s evidence of another volcanic province that roughly lines up with this time interval,” Gill said. “But we’re in the very beginning of trying to understand what happened.”
Ancient oxygen losses echo in modern oceans
The ancient rock record also offers a way to examine the potential consequences of environmental changes unfolding today. Modern oceans are experiencing rising temperatures, acidification, and declining oxygen levels.
Ocean deoxygenation
is an ongoing concern, including in coastal environments such as the
Chesapeake Bay
Although the ancient and modern circumstances are different, understanding how warming and oxygen depletion affected marine life in the past could help scientists anticipate the combined pressures facing ocean ecosystems today.
“Earth has run this experiment in the past. We have evidence that the climate gets warmer, and then all these other knock-on effects come afterwards,” Gill said. “It gives us some sense of what we can expect to happen.”
Reference: “Deoxygenation in the equatorial Panthalassan Ocean predated the end-Triassic mass extinction” by Kayla E. McCabe, Selva M. Marroquín, Andrew H. Caruthers, Jeremy D. Owens, Martyn L. Golding, Rachel E. B. Reid, Theodore R. Them II, João P. Trabucho-Alexandre, Yorick P. Veenma and Benjamin C. Gill, April 01 2026,
Communications Earth & Environment
DOI: 10.1038/s43247-026-03362-w

title: Scientists Discover a Powerful New Way To Destroy Toxic “Forever Chemicals”
content:
Chemistry
A palladium-coated membrane uses hydrogen to help break down PFAS “forever chemicals.” Credit: Graphic by Jason Drees
A new water-treatment technology could offer a breakthrough in the fight against forever chemicals.
Scientists have developed a new way to destroy toxic “forever chemicals” in water rather than simply filter them out. During a 58-day experiment, the system removed more than 90% of each of six PFAS compounds and stripped away approximately 83% of their fluorine, providing evidence that the pollutants were being chemically broken down.
PFAS are widely used in nonstick cookware, waterproof clothing, food packaging, and firefighting foam. Their exceptional durability also allows them to persist in soil, water, wildlife, and the human body. Exposure to certain PFAS has been linked to cancer, thyroid disorders, immune system problems, and reproductive health risks.
Breaking Down Nearly Indestructible Chemicals
Conventional treatments capture PFAS using filters, membranes, or other materials, leaving contaminated waste that must still be managed. Researchers at Arizona State University and their collaborators instead developed a system that attacks the chemicals’ molecular structure.
“PFAS are hard to break down, and normal processes that we use don’t work,” said Bruce Rittmann, director of the Biodesign Swette Center for Environmental Biotechnology.
The challenge lies in the carbon-fluorine bonds that make PFAS exceptionally stable. “It’s called the strongest bond in organic chemistry,” Rittmann said. With fluorine atoms shielding the carbon backbone, ordinary degradation processes struggle to attack the molecules. “There’s really no place to get a start to break it down,” he explained.
A New Way to Destroy PFAS
The researchers created tiny membrane fibers coated with palladium nanoparticles. Hydrogen gas travels through the fibers to the palladium, which activates the hydrogen and helps it break carbon-fluorine bonds in PFAS molecules approaching from the surrounding water.
“The palladium attracts the PFAS molecule, and the palladium attracts the hydrogen and puts them together,” Rittmann said.
The system builds on earlier membrane technology that supplies hydrogen to pollutant-degrading bacteria. In the new approach, palladium replaces the microbes. During continuous testing, the technology successfully treated all six PFAS compounds examined. “We showed that this mechanism worked for all six,” Rittmann said. “It’s a universal mechanism.”
The findings were published in the
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Tackling a Widespread Environmental Threat
PFAS contamination affects groundwater, wastewater, soil, and food supplies. Particularly high concentrations occur near landfills, airports, military bases, and facilities where PFAS-containing firefighting foams have been used.
“We all have PFAS in us,” Rittmann said. “They stay in the environment. They move up the food chain, and so they’re a big legacy problem.”
What Comes Next?
Although the 58-day test demonstrated sustained treatment, scaling up the technology presents challenges, particularly the cost of palladium. “Palladium is expensive,” Rittmann said. “It’s around $50,000 a kilogram” (about $22,700 per pound).
The researchers are working to reduce palladium requirements and explore combining the technology with existing filtration systems. They are also developing hybrid membranes that pair palladium with pollutant-degrading bacteria, allowing contaminants to be attacked through different mechanisms. “We’ve shown that this works too,” Rittmann said.
Reference: “Catalytic reactive-hydrogen membranes for rapid capture and hydrodefluorination of six PFAS of regulatory concern” by Min Long, Ai-Shi Wang, Welman C. Elias, Chen Zhou, Thomas P. Senftle, Michael S. Wong, Jie Cheng and Bruce E. Rittmann, 19 October 2026,
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2613985123

title: A Simple Tongue Exercise Could Hold the Key to Fighting the Devastating Effects of ALS
content:
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease, is a progressive neurological disorder that damages motor neurons, the nerve cells responsible for controlling voluntary muscle movements. As these neurons deteriorate, people experience increasing muscle weakness, eventually affecting their ability to walk, speak, swallow, and breathe. Credit: Shutterstock
Researchers at the University of Missouri have uncovered a promising way to help surviving nerve cells compensate for damage caused by ALS and other motor neuron diseases.
The loss of tongue control in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) can affect far more than speech. It can make swallowing increasingly difficult and interfere with breathing during sleep. Now, researchers at the University of Missouri have discovered that tongue exercise can increase the activity of surviving nerve cells in a preclinical model, potentially offering a new approach to preserving these essential functions.
ALS, also called Lou Gehrig’s disease, progressively damages the motor neurons responsible for muscle movement and currently has no cure. However, not all neurons controlling the tongue are lost, particularly during the early stages. Researchers are investigating whether these surviving cells can compensate for damaged neurons and help maintain muscle function.
How Exercise Helps Surviving Nerve Cells
The findings center on neuroplasticity, the nervous system’s ability to adapt to damage or changing conditions. In the preclinical model, tongue exercise increased the activity of surviving motor neurons, suggesting that targeted training may help the remaining cells compensate for those lost to disease. Scientists have not yet determined exactly how exercise produces this response.
Dr. Nichols Credit: University of Missouri
“This adaptation is called neuroplasticity, meaning the nervous system changes how it operates to compensate for damage, and this finding offers hope for those with motor neuron diseases,” said Nicole Nichols, an associate professor in the College of Veterinary Medicine and coauthor of the study. “By boosting the activity of the surviving neurons, we can help preserve the quality of life for those with ALS, spinal muscular atrophy and other motor neuron diseases.”
Why Preserving Tongue Function Matters
The tongue plays a central role in speaking, moving food during swallowing, and keeping the airway open during sleep. As the muscles weaken in people with ALS, eating can become difficult enough to require a feeding tube. Reduced tongue muscle function can also contribute to sleep apnea, a condition in which breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.
“For those with ALS, preserving swallowing function not only reduces the chance of developing sleep apnea, it could also mean the difference between needing a feeding tube or continuing to eat normally,” she said. “That’s incredibly meaningful for quality of life.”
Could Future Treatments Reproduce the Effects of Exercise?
Although the results are promising, the benefits have so far been demonstrated only in a preclinical model. Researchers now want to understand the biological mechanisms that allow tongue exercise to increase neuronal activity. Identifying those mechanisms could eventually support the development of medications that reproduce the effects of exercise without requiring patients to perform physical training.
“If we can figure out exactly how and why the tongue exercise helps the remaining neurons function better, that can help the development of treatments that mimic the benefits,” Nichols said. “For example, for someone with a very poor prognosis who may not be able to do tongue exercise, is there an injectable that we can give them that would activate those surviving motor neurons to improve their function? While both tongue exercise as a therapy and an injectable would require human clinical trials in the future, this finding is a step in the right direction.”
Nichols and her colleagues hope to advance tongue exercise toward human clinical trials within the next several years through collaborations at Mizzou’s NextGen Precision Health.
Reference: “Impact of tongue exercise on hypoglossal axis survival, structure, and output in a rodent model of hypoglossal motor neuron degeneration” by Amy N. Nichols, 12 May 2026,
Journal of Neurophysiology

title: Why Are Men Twice As Likely To Develop Parkinson’s? Scientists Discover a Hidden Clue in the Brain
content:
Parkinson’s disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement, coordination, and other brain functions. It develops as dopamine-producing nerve cells become damaged or die, leading to symptoms such as tremors, stiffness, slowed movement, and balance problems. Credit: Shutterstock
Scientists have identified sex-specific differences in gene activity within brain cells that may help explain why Parkinson’s disease affects men more frequently than women.
Men are 1.5 to 2 times more likely than women to develop Parkinson’s disease, yet the biological reasons remain poorly understood. New research suggests that differences in gene activity within the brain’s support cells may help explain why the condition affects the sexes differently.
The findings, presented at the Federation of European Neuroscience Societies (FENS) Forum 2026, are based on brain tissue from 73 people with Parkinson’s disease (28 women and 45 men) and 24 people without the condition (9 women and 15 men). Researchers examined five brain regions, identifying cellular changes shared by both sexes as well as distinct patterns in men and women.
Brain Support Cells Reveal Sex-Specific Differences
The strongest differences appeared in two types of glial cells, which support and protect neurons. In astrocytes, gene activity related to mitochondria, the structures that produce cellular energy, differed between sexes. In oligodendrocytes, researchers identified differences involving genes responsible for producing and maintaining myelin, the protective coating surrounding nerve fibers. These patterns appeared across the brain regions studied.
Professor Julia Schulze-Hentrich of Saarland University in Germany, who led the research, explained: “We looked at differences in gene expression individually in all cells of the brain – neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia – in healthy brains and in PD brains in men and women. We studied five brain regions and found that PD causes common changes in the brain, regardless of sex. All these cells in the five regions, showed signs of being under stress. They switched on proteins that help damaged proteins fold correctly, called ‘chaperones’. However, we also found important differences between men and women in gene activity in some cells and some brain regions.”
“This shows that PD triggers some shared ‘stress responses’ in everyone’s brain cells, but also there are differences between men and women at the cellular level, especially in how the brain ‘support’ cells manage energy and protect nerve connections. Our findings help to explain why symptoms and disease progression in Parkinson’s differ between men and women. Eventually, they may lead to more personalized treatments rather than treating all patients with PD as biologically identical,” said Prof. Schulze-Hentrich.
Why Parkinson’s Affects Men More Often
Parkinson’s disease causes progressive brain damage and affects approximately 9.4 million people worldwide. About 90% of cases are thought to involve a combination of genetic variation and environmental or lifestyle influences. Men not only develop the disease more frequently but also tend to experience faster cognitive decline and worsening difficulties with everyday activities.
“The higher prevalence of Parkinson’s disease in men suggests that sex-dependent biology may influence vulnerability. Therefore, studying sex differences may help identifying disease mechanisms that would be hidden in analyses that pool men and women together,” said Prof. Schulze-Hentrich, who is affiliated with Saarland University’s Center for Gender-Specific Biology and Medicine (CGMB).
Earlier Research Linked Parkinson’s to DNA Changes
The investigation builds on an earlier study involving 71 agricultural workers with early Parkinson’s and 147 healthy participants. Researchers found changes in DNA methylation across 69 genomic regions in women with Parkinson’s, compared with just two in men. DNA methylation regulates gene activity without altering the underlying DNA sequence, functioning much like a dimmer switch.
“These findings suggested that a person’s genetic makeup influences these DNA methylation changes, and that interaction with environmental exposures, such as to pesticides, may also contribute to the development of Parkinson’s disease,” Prof. Schulze-Hentrich said.
The new study extended this work by examining gene expression in individual types of brain cells. Although it identified differences associated with biological sex, it did not establish that those differences directly cause the higher rate of Parkinson’s in men.
Toward More Personalized Parkinson’s Care
The study’s relatively small sample size limits its conclusions, and larger investigations are needed. The findings also reinforce the need to examine men and women separately in Parkinson’s research, which has historically focused heavily on neurons and male subjects.
“Most importantly, our results indicate that it is crucial to recognize that biology varies between the sexes in PD research and that, wherever possible, researchers should analyze data separately in males and females instead of pooling everyone together. This is crucial to see whether an association, effect or outcome differs by sex. It also helps identify gaps in evidence because many studies still underreport or pool sex-specific outcomes.
“For patients, the main benefit is more personalized care, as sex-specific analysis can help clinicians predict which symptoms are more likely, monitor problems earlier, and choose treatments that fit a patient’s risk profile better.”
A new German research initiative aims to investigate how sex-related differences in glial cells affect neurological disease.
“Investigating how male- and female-specific glial responses shape vulnerability, progression and treatment response is rarely done in a systematic and coordinated way. Therefore, the German Research Foundation (DFG) Priority Programme ‘SEX and GLIA’ starting in the autumn of 2026 will bring together physiologists with functional geneticists and computational biologists to uncover a largely hidden layer of sex-biased biology that previous studies often ignored,” Prof. Schulze-Hentrich concluded.
Understanding the Role of Brain Support Cells
Professor Christina Dalla of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, Greece, who chairs the FENS Forum communication committee and was not involved in the research, highlighted how the findings build on earlier investigations of environmental exposures.
“Although we have known for some time that there are higher rates of Parkinson’s disease in men than in women, it is interesting to see how Professor Schulze-Hentrich and her colleagues have built on their earlier work studying the impact of pesticides on agricultural workers to investigate the changes that occur at the cellular level and to understand the mechanisms underlying the development of Parkinson’s disease.
“Their findings show that although some changes in genetic activity are the same in both sexes, there are others that only occur in men, or in women. This is an important finding because it shows that there are differences in glial cells, the ‘support’ cells in the brain that are associated with the onset of the disease, and that these could interact with other factors such as sex, hormones, or social or environmental exposures.”

content:
为什么下一轮太阳能成本曲线，可能取决于部署架构，而不是又一个孤立环节
过去二十年的大部分时间里，太阳能行业一直在逐个环节地降本。组件效率更高、价格更低，逆变器更智能，支架系统更轻、更优化。但项目交付和组装的方式，变化却小得多。
一个典型项目仍然围绕分别选型的产品、项目专属物料清单，以及大量必须在现场解决的决策来组织。随着硬件成本下降，这种部署复杂性在剩余降本空间里占的比重越来越大。
下一轮有意义的太阳能降本，可能来自改变优化单元——从单个环节转向完整安装过程。
制造系统靠重复既定单元来实现规模化。相比之下，太阳能施工往往从一长串零件清单开始规划，之后才转化为安装顺序。把这一逻辑反过来会很有力量：先定义可重复的现场单元，再围绕它设计结构、接口、包装和作业指导。
合适的单元会因项目而异。它可能是一小块屋顶区域、一个跟踪支架单元、一个固定倾角支架单元，或另一个可重复的工作块。重点不是把同一种几何形式强加到每个项目上，而是建立一个稳定的单元，围绕它来组织人力、物料流、质量检查和自动化。
现场每一个决策都会增加时间和出错的可能：哪个零件装到哪里，哪个紧固件对应哪个连接，某个部件是否缺失，某个接口应如何调整。有些变量不可避免。现场荷载、地形、土壤、基础和当地规范要求，仍然需要项目专属工程设计。
但许多组装决策可以前移到设计、制造和包装环节。可重复的几何形式、受控的物料清单、预配置的子组件和清晰的安装顺序，能让现场施工人员执行一个已知流程，而不是在每一排都重新揣摩设计者的意图。
这就是系统套件方法的核心承诺：不是一箱装了更多产品的盒子，而是一种更早决定后续事情该如何发生的方法。
把接口当作架构来设计
标准化安装单元只有在接口可预测时才有用。组件与结构之间的连接、结构件之间的关系，以及基础与地上工作之间的交接，都会影响现场流程能变得多可重复。
因此，接口值得被当作架构来设计，而不是作为附带硬件来选用。设计良好的接口能管理公差、提供清晰的荷载路径、减少散件、便于检查，并让正确的组装状态一目了然。这些特性今天有利于人工安装，将来也能支撑机器人安装。
更广泛的启示是，标准化应集中在边界上。应用场景专属的结构可以保持不同，但共享一致的规则，规定组件、部件、工具和质量控制系统如何与它们衔接。
把包装纳入工程设计
包装通常被视为系统设计完成后的物流任务。在以部署为中心的模型里，包装成为安装架构的一部分。
物料应按其被使用的顺序和数量到达。托盘尺寸、部件尺寸、安装单元尺寸和项目排程应相互协调。备件数量和损坏恢复流程应经过刻意规划，而不是临时应付。目标不仅是降低运费，更是减少现场的搬运次数、寻找、重新包装和在制品。
当包装围绕现场工序来设计时，工厂与工地之间的边界会更清晰。更多准备工作可以在受控条件下完成，而现场则成为进行可重复最终组装的地方。
采购的是结果，不是一堆零件
系统思维也能改变采购。逐件采购让每个零件都可见，但也可能掩盖这些零件之间协调的成本。缺失五金件、公差不相容、质保碎片化和现场返工，很少体现在最低的分项价格里。
相反，系统套件可以作为一个明确的部署结果来评估：一定可重复数量的装机容量，连同必要的接口、结构件、文档和物料流一起交付。这并不会消除成本透明度或竞争，而是改变商业单元，使供应商因降低整体安装复杂性而获得回报，而不仅仅是因为某个组件的重量或价格更低。
标准化，但不僵化
对系统套件最强烈的反对意见是：太阳能项目太因场地而异，难以标准化。如果标准化意味着把每个项目强行塞进同一种物理设计，这个反对意见是成立的。但如果标准化意味着定义可复用的规则、接口和部署单元，同时在条件需要时保留项目专属工程设计，那么这个反对意见就不那么有说服力。
一个有用的平台，会把应重复的部分和必须适配的部分分开。组件搬运、连接逻辑、包装惯例、检查标准和作业指导可以在许多项目中重复。基础、构件尺寸、防腐和荷载工况则可以适配。设计挑战在于智能地划定这条边界。
自动化常被当作一个独立的技术问题来讨论：机器能否打桩、搬运组件或安装紧固件？系统套件视角则提出一个更早的问题：产品是否已经被组织好，使机器能够可靠地与它交互？
机器人受益于那些同样能提高人工生产率的特性——可预测的呈现方式、宽松的对齐公差、少量散件、简单动作和可验证的完成状态。标准化部署架构不能保证自动化实现，但它创造了条件，使自动化能够超越演示阶段、实现规模化。
下一轮太阳能成本曲线
太阳能硬件会继续进步。然而，竞争力将越来越取决于完整系统从设计到采购、包装和现场组装的流转效率。
这提示了一组不同的开发问题：
· 哪些现场决策可以更早、在控制更好的条件下解决？
· 项目应围绕哪个可重复安装单元来组织？
· 即使支撑结构不同，哪些接口也应保持通用？
· 包装和物料流应如何反映实际施工顺序？
· 现在必须标准化什么，才能支撑未来更高程度的自动化？
太阳能产业的下一个重大进步，可能不会来自又一个独立环节，而会来自让整个系统更容易交付、组装、验证和维护。
Jian Yuan博士是光伏结构系统开发商，也是 ModuRack, LLC 创始人兼首席执行官。他的工作聚焦于太阳能施工的系统架构、部署和自动化。

政策分类路径: 政策 > 监管落实型政策 > 正外部性 > 可再生能源优惠 > 机制（电）价
政策分类依据: 河北发布2027年度新能源机制电价竞价方案，核心是机制电价的形成与执行规则
content:
2026年10月21日，河北省发展和改革委员会同日印发两份核心文件：《河北省进一步深化新能源上网电价市场化改革增量新能源项目竞价工作方案》(冀发改能价〔2026〕993号)与《关于2027年度新能源机制电价竞价工作有关事项的通知》(冀发改能价〔2026〕994号)。前者为竞价规则的整体性修订，后者明确2027年度具体竞价参数，两份文件共同构成河北新能源机制电价竞价的最新政策框架，也是河北南网与冀北电网竞价规则首次实现省级层面统一规范。
本次调整呈现“降门槛、提精度、统规则”三大特征：准入端取消履约保函，替换为承诺书制，大幅减轻中小投资商的资金占用压力，申报流程简化为一段式申报;规则端出清集中度约束门槛从30%提高至50%，边际报价策略空间收窄，倒逼申报电量更贴近真实交付能力;体系端南北网竞价流程、价格上限、执行期限全面并轨，结束此前两网各自为政的规则格局。同时2027年度机制电量总规模定为600.10亿千瓦时，竞价上下限统一为0.2—0.36元/千瓦时，并明确大型工商业
、绿电直连项目上网电量不纳入机制电价范围。
需要特别注意的是，规则统一并不等同于收益趋同。当前河北南网电力现货市场已转入正式运行，分时价格完全由市场形成;冀北电网仍处于模拟试运行阶段，两网在差价结算方向、现货价格结构上已出现明显分化，同一套规则下南北项目的收益逻辑将持续存在差异。
为帮助新能源投资商、项目开发商、聚合商与售电公司完整吃透两份新规、厘清南北网差异、优化报价策略、规避申报风险，索比光伏网结合文件原文、河北电力市场运行数据及历史竞价情况，推出深度解读报告，覆盖规则逐条修订对照、年度参数拆解、主体范围边界界定、南北市场分化分析、分主体实操建议、风险提示等全维度内容。

11月2日，可再生能源法修订草案提请十四届全国人大常委会第二十五次会议初次审议。
发展可再生能源，是改善能源结构、保障能源安全、建设能源强国和推进生态文明建设的重要任务。党的十八大以来，我国可再生能源发展取得历史性成就，实现历史性变革，构建了全球最大、发展最快的可再生能源体系。
修订草案共十章七十六条，主要修改内容包括：明确加强党的领导，完善立法目的和有关要求，完善资源调查与发展规划，加强可再生能源开发建设管理，加强可再生能源生产与输送管理，健全市场交易与价格机制，强化消纳责任与消费促进，完善科技创新与产业发展，强化保障与监督，完善法律责任。

title: Stillstrom completes testing of offshore vessel charging system
content:
Stillstrom, part of Maersk, has completed the construction and factory
acceptance testing of its new Vessel Container Unit (VCU), marking a key
milestone for the offshore charging technology developer.
The company said the VCU is the world's first connection solution that
enables a Service Operation Vessel (SOV) to charge its battery directly
“High-voltage power has never been transferred to a vessel offshore in
this way, and the connector package inside our VCU represents several years
of careful development and testing,” said Graeme Wood, Managing Director
of Stillstrom UK.
“The control system and integrated safety interlocks significantly reduce
the risks associated with offshore charging for both vessel owners and
wind farm operators."
The milestone marks the next phase of the project, moving from simulations
to fully tested hardware. The VCU contains an 11kV connector package and
features a modular design intended to support seamless charging and control
interfaces for vessels operating offshore.
According to the company, the complete charging system is expected to be
ready for extended offshore sea trials by next year.

title: Nova Scotia and Vermont explore new transmission routes to strengthen New England grid
content:
Nova Scotia and Vermont explore new transmission routes to strengthen New England grid TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Nova Scotia and Vermont explore new transmission routes to strengthen New England grid
Vermont and Nova Scotia have signed a three-year agreement focused on transmission
collaboration and regional grid integration as electricity demand continues
to grow across New England.
The memorandum of understanding (MoU) is designed to create opportunities
to deliver Nova Scotia's offshore wind resources to New England, helping
to strengthen grid reliability and enhance energy security.
“As a small state, we can’t generate affordable, clean and reliable energy
alone, which is why regional partnerships are critical to reaching our
goals,” said Vermont Gov. Phil Scott.
“This agreement with Vermont is another important step as we build connections
with energy partners, advance Wind West and position Nova Scotia to become
a clean energy superpower,” said Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston.
Under the agreement, Nova Scotia and Vermont will explore new transmission
pathways, including a potential expansion of the bidirectional transmission
link and upgrades to the Highgate Converter Station, to support the export
of Nova Scotia offshore wind energy to New England.

title: Port of Raahe and Buss Ports sign offshore wind partnership
content:
The Port of Raahe and Buss Ports have signed a memorandum of understanding
(MoU) to support offshore wind development in the Gulf of Bothnia.
Under the agreement, the two organisations will assess infrastructure requirements,
engage with key stakeholders and explore how best to support future offshore
wind projects in the region.
The partnership aims to strengthen the Port of Raahe's position as a preferred
hub for offshore wind activities in Finland and the wider Gulf of Bothnia
The agreement comes as the offshore wind sector continues to evolve, increasing
demand for suitable infrastructure and logistics partners to support efficient
project delivery.
Seppo Vehkaoja, Managing Director of the Port of Raahe said: “collaborating
with Buss Ports, we are now combining strong local infrastructure with
extensive expertise in offshore wind logistics – creating an attractive
offering for future projects in the Gulf of Bothnia.”
“Together, we aim to contribute to developing suitable port and logistics
solutions for future offshore wind projects,”said Managing Director
of Buss Port Logistics, Claas Pinkenburg.

title: Taihan renames cable-laying vessel to strengthen brand
content:
Taihan Cable & Solution has officially renamed its cable-laying vessel
(CLV) Skandi Connector to Taihan Connector. The company said this change
is intended to strengthen brand recognition in the global submarine cable
market and align the vessel more closely with its corporate identity.
The new name retains the "Connector" element from the vessel’s
previous identity, preserving the recognition it has established during
operations in international markets.
Having worked on 27 projects and installed around 1,300 km of submarine
cables, the vessel was acquired by Taihan Cable & Solution from DOF
Group back in May 2026.
The 11,000 ton class vessel can carry up to 7,000 tons of submarine cable
and is designed to support offshore wind inter-array and export cable installation,
as well as long-distance interconnection and HVDC cable projects.
The company now operates South Korea’s only two-vessel CLV fleet dedicated
to offshore wind projects, comprising PALOS and Taihan Connector.
Taihan said the fleet enables it to deploy vessels according to project
requirements and installation conditions while supporting turnkey delivery
across the submarine cable value chain.

title: NKT secures three long-term framework agreements with N1
content:
NKT has been awarded three framework agreements by N1 to supply low- and
medium-voltage power cables of up to 72 kV. The agreements will run for
six years, with the option of two one year extensions.
Under the contracts, NKT will deliver between 700 km and 1,000 km of power
cables annually. The company said the agreements strengthen its long-term
partnership with Danish distribution system operator N1.
The project is intended to support the expansion and modernisation of Denmark's
electricity grid at a time when investment in power infrastructure is becoming
increasingly important to meet rising electricity demand.
"Distribution grids are a fundamental part of the energy transition,
and the significant investments planned in Denmark over the coming years
underline the need for reliable power cable capacity and strong, long-term
partnerships," said Carlos Fernandez, executive vice president and
head of Distribution at NKT.
"With our expanded production capabilities in Asnæs and our broader
European manufacturing footprint, NKT is well positioned to support N1
as it continues to develop the electricity grid for a more electrified
future."

title: Scotland's renewable energy sector supports 49,200 jobs, study finds
content:
Scottish Renewables has announced that Scotland's renewable energy sector
supported approximately 49,200 full-time equivalent (FTE) jobs in 2024,
with offshore wind accounting for the largest share at 18,800 jobs. Onshore
wind followed closely, supporting 17,825 FTE positions.
The study, conducted by the University of Strathclyde's Fraser of Allander
Institute and commissioned by Scottish Renewables, also estimated that
the sector generated £14.9 billion in economic output during 2024.
According to the report, four major developments contributed to the sector's
economic impact: the South Kyle Wind Farm, the Seagreen
Offshore Wind Farm,
Sumitomo Electric's subsea cable factory and exploratory works at the Coire
Glas pumped storage hydropower project.
Angela Hepworth, CEO of Scottish Renewables, said: "These figures

title: AI Agenda Live: EY Consulting on Bringing AI ROI to your P&L
content:
Partner Content
AI Agenda Live: EY Consulting on Bringing AI ROI to your P&L
[email protected]
Profile and archive
The capabilities AI
can bring to companies seem limitless. So do AI token bills, which have skyrocketed, pressuring CFOs and boards to show that such spending can actually boost revenue or profits.
Dan Diasio, EY Global AI Leader and Consulting CTO
, has led teams advising the world’s largest companies on their AI transformations.
The Information
According to Diasio, rising token costs haven’t dampened enterprise enthusiasm for AI. But enthusiasm alone isn’t enough to move profit margins. To underscore this point, he referred to two surveys suggesting that many organizations believe AI is paying off, but few can yet trace those returns in their financial results. The first, conducted by
The Information
, found that a third of organizations reported getting a return from AI that was a multiple of what they spend on it. The second, an EY survey conducted as part of
the EY CEO Imperative Series
, found that only 11% of CEOs say their companies link AI impact to financial reporting and review it regularly at the senior management level.
“There’s value in increasing productivity, and there’s the value organizations need to be able to prove in their [profit and loss statement], and those are two different things,” Diasio said. “Many organizations I talk to would say AI is significantly increasing productivity. But when the CFO looks at the investment, that productivity needs to translate into two things: Are we making more revenue, and are we taking costs out of the organization?”
Thinking beyond use cases
What this means is that business leaders have to devise more concrete plans for AI  than they did in past cycles.
“I’m seeing this big pivot from ‘let’s go identify some use cases’ to using AI to drive business transformation,” he said.
To illustrate the point, Diasio described how a consumer products company could use AI to cut the time from product idea to market from 18 months to three, a move that would drive revenue by bringing more products to market faster.
“That’s the sort of change that enterprises need to see to be all in,” he said.
The agent handoff
As part of that transformation, organizations are rethinking the relationship between human employees and so-called AI agents and, in many cases, finding unique ways to use agents to create value. Diasio pointed to banks, which have started using agents to assist financial advisors and streamline back-office work. The real value, he said, is in how those AI-assisted touch points build the bank’s relationships with clients and hopefully pay off by  helping it generate more revenue.
“They’re using a lot of these AI capabilities not as a way of reducing costs, but of building brand,” he said of the banks.
Starting fresh
Ultimately, making AI’s payoff visible in financial results is going to require organizations to think of AI less as a technology rollout and more as a driver of measurable results. That means redesigning whole business functions from the ground up, not just automating pieces of them.
“Fast-forward 12 months and companies are going to start thinking about new ways to run their business in parts,” he said. “That means doing the hard thing: addressing the processes that need to be entirely rebuilt.”
That’s a harder path than simply adopting new tools, he said, but it’s the one that actually shows up on the P&L.
The views reflected in this article are the views of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of Ernst & Young LLP or other members of the global EY organization.

title: Anthropic Touts Claude’s Chip Design Skills to IPO Investors
content: Anthropic’s AI models have helped uncover serious cyber vulnerabilities and transform the software coding profession. Now the company is seeing just how much of an advantage its models can give it in unfamiliar terrain: designing its own AI chips. The company, which is barreling toward an initial public offering later this month that could value it around $1.5 trillion, has told investors in recent meetings that its new 15-person chip design team is already using its own Claude models for engineering and design work on its custom chips, according to four people familiar with the discussions. Its engineers have found Claude cuts down the time it takes to design chips compared to their estimates of traditional workflows at large chip designers such as Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, said some of the people. The efforts come as rival OpenAI has been highlighting chip design as a potential source of revenue. OpenAI’s chief financial officer, Sarah Friar, said at a Goldman Sachs conference in September that chip design is among the business sectors it is targeting, alongside financial services and life sciences. She said the ChatGPT maker is relying on its own frontier AI models to design its Jalapeño custom chip, which it plans to start using in significant quantities next year. Both companies have largely focused on how AI could improve the way chips run and train their own models. It’s not clear how they will achieve that, or how the companies plan to turn such advances into products for their customers. Anthropic hasn’t disclosed any plans to commercialize its AI for chip design. Still, helping customers design and test chips using AI represents a potentially huge market for both companies. Publicly traded Synopsys and Cadence Design Systems both sell software and other services to help chip engineers design, simulate and test different semiconductor chips, circuit boards and electronics systems before they are manufactured. The two companies are expected to generate a combined $16 billion for their current fiscal years. But the custom chip efforts of Anthropic and OpenAI could potentially stoke tensions with some of their biggest backers, which also supply them with chips via cloud computing contracts or directly with data centers. Anthropic uses chips made by Amazon, Google, Nvidia and AMD, which have committed to investing about $90 billion altogether into the startup. If Anthropic or OpenAI end up making AI models that are far better at chip design than others’ models, they could also keep the most cutting-edge versions of those models to themselves, at least at first, giving them a leg up over other chip design firms. Anthropic’s efforts to use Claude for chip design follow the company’s August announcement that it is building an in-house team to design ​custom chips to train and run its Claude AI models. It previously held talks with Samsung Electronics as a potential manufacturing partner, The Information reported . It can take years to develop new chips, largely due to the tedious effort of testing and verifying different potential designs that could involve trillions of tiny circuits. But OpenAI said it took just nine months to develop Jalapeño with Broadcom using OpenAI’s most advanced models. And executives at startups that aim to use AI to speed up chip design said AI might be able to cut the time needed to design a fully functioning chip to a few months—or eventually even less time. “Hardware design is difficult and unforgiving—exactly the sort of domain we want Claude to excel at,” wrote Anthropic in a posting for a research engineer to advance its models’ silicon-design abilities. Anthropic’s models have proven the most adept at design by one measure. According to a benchmark released by startup ChipAgents and Nvidia last month that aims to measure how good various AI models are at chip design, Claude Fable 5.1 scored the best. That said, there still seems to be a long way to go for AI to fully take over chip design workflows; the model scored 16.6% on the test. If Anthropic eventually decides to sell its AI to help other companies design chips, such Claude-based tools would compete with Cadence and Synopsys, which develop electronic design automation software. (OpenAI in September announced a multiyear agreement to develop a model specialized for using Synopsys’ tools for semiconductor design.) One executive at a startup selling AI tools for chip design said Anthropic has approached some EDA companies asking to buy or otherwise use some of their chip design data—presumably to help make its models better at chip design. Still, it may be an uphill battle for Anthropic to convince some of the larger EDA or chip manufacturing companies to use its models across all stages of the chip design process. Due to potential privacy concerns, the highly secretive chip companies may prefer to run instances of open-source models on their own hardware.
